title: Audit Finding Closure Rate Trending
exclusions: Controls within their defined testing cadence; newly implemented controls in maturation period; framework version transition gaps during documented migration; formally accepted residual risks with governance approval.
evidence: Control effectiveness report showing assessment dates, testing results, evidence links, finding status, and management review decisions archived for certification audit evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=grc` sourcetype='grc:audit_finding' where `entity` satisfies detection threshold for UC-22.9.2 ('Audit Finding Closure Rate Trending'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.

app: Splunk Add-on for ServiceNow (Splunkbase 1928), Splunk DB Connect for GRC findings, or custom `grc:audit_finding` HEC
spl:
index=grc OR index=compliance sourcetype="grc:audit_finding" earliest=-90d
| eval is_closed=if(match(status,"(?i)closed|resolved|verified"),1,0)
| eval finding_key=coalesce(finding_id,uuid,ticket_id,number)
| timechart span=1d dc(eval(if(is_closed=0,finding_key,null()))) as open_findings
    dc(eval(if(is_closed=1,finding_key,null()))) as distinct_closed_entities
| trendline sma7(open_findings) as open_smoothed
| predict open_findings as open_forecast algorithm=LLP future_timespan=14
description: Trending open versus closed audit findings over ninety days makes backlog and closure velocity visible before external audits, while mean time to remediate highlights whether remediation playbooks and ownership are working.
value: Trending open versus closed audit findings over ninety days makes backlog and closure velocity visible befo.... Timely UC-22.9.2 alerting on 'Audit Finding Closure Rate Trending' reduces audit findings, regulatory gaps, and attestation delays before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: (1) Ensure each finding emits at least one event with stable `finding_key` and transition events or daily snapshots for `status`; (2) normalize `closed_time` to epoch seconds; (3) if only snapshot data exists, switch `dc()` panels to `latest()` by key in a summary index; (4) alert when `open_forecast` rises week over week or when `mean_mttr_days` exceeds your SLA; (5) export MTTR trend for audit workpapers. Indexes required: `index=compliance`, `index=grc`; Sourcetypes: `sourcetype=grc:audit_finding`.
visualization: Dual-axis line (open vs closed counts), area chart (`open_smoothed`), line chart (`mean_mttr_days`, `mttr_trend`, `mttr_forecast`), single value (`wow_mttr_pct`).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Authorised ISO 27001 control testing** — Internal audit exercises 'Audit Finding Closure Rate Trending' (UC-22.9.2) on `entity` during scheduled clause A.5.36 sampling. Match compliance programme calendar.

2. **External assessor sampling** — QSA activity spikes `index=grc` `grc:audit_finding` without crossing evidence threshold. Cross-check engagement letter in `iso_27001_exception_register.csv`.

3. **Planned maintenance affecting control telemetry** — CAB change pauses ingestion to `grc` for `entity`. Compare `_time` with active change record.

4. **Third-party processor under contract** — BAA/DPA-covered vendor generates expected rows grouped by `entity` during normal service delivery.

**Suppression mechanism:** `iso_27001_exception_register.csv` keyed on `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`, joined before alert threshold.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Enterprise ≥9.2 or Splunk Cloud (current). Scheduling requires a search head not under memory pressure (check `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=ProcessRunner` for OOM warnings before deploying a new scheduled search).
• **Indexes**: `grc`, `compliance` must exist on all indexers with retention matching the regulation's minimum (PCI: 1y, HIPAA: 6y, NIST 800-53: 1-3y per FIPS 199, SOX: 7y). Set `frozenTimePeriodInSecs` accordingly in `indexes.conf`.
• **Regulatory mapping**: This detection evidences clause `A.5.36`. The control objective is: "Evidence that ISO 27001 A.5.36 is enforced — Splunk UC-22.9.2: Audit Finding Closure Rate Trending." — every alert payload should include this text so downstream consumers know the compliance purpose.

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Data collection is bespoke for this UC — no single canonical TA parses every source the detection relies on. Route data into `grc`, `compliance` under `grc:audit_finding`, and document the ingestion path in the UC runbook so future engineers know where each field originates.


5 operational considerations apply to the rollout of this detection:


• **Hint 1:** Ensure each finding emits at least one event with stable `finding_key` and transition events or daily snapshots for `status`. This is an operational consideration that influences either the detection's accuracy or its maintainability — document the approach chosen in the UC runbook.

• **Hint 2:** normalize `closed_time` to epoch seconds. Field normalisation mismatches are one of the top silent-failure modes in enrichment-driven detections — invest in automated tests that assert key-match rates after every TA upgrade.

• **Hint 3:** if only snapshot data exists, switch `dc()` panels to `latest()` by key in a summary index. This is an operational consideration that influences either the detection's accuracy or its maintainability — document the approach chosen in the UC runbook.

• **Hint 4:** alert when `open_forecast` rises week over week or when `mean_mttr_days` exceeds your SLA. This is an operational consideration that influences either the detection's accuracy or its maintainability — document the approach chosen in the UC runbook.

• **Hint 5:** export MTTR trend for audit workpapers. Report-generation cadence must match the regulatory reporting cycle; a monthly digest satisfies an annual review requirement but not a quarterly one.

## Step 2 — Implement the search

`streamstats` computes a running aggregate over events in sequence, preserving event order. For "Audit Finding Closure Rate Trending" specifically, this is the right choice because the control asks a temporal question — detecting accelerating trends, windowed thresholds, or deviations from a rolling baseline.

For "Audit Finding Closure Rate Trending," the aggregation exposes temporal structure that a single point-in-time reading cannot — the compliance question is about behaviour over a period, not at an instant.

The grouping `by the grouping fields` is the analytical unit — the aggregate is computed within each distinct combination. A common mistake is grouping by a field that has cardinality near 1:1 with events, which produces a group-per-event and makes the window stat trivially equal to the event value.

Order sensitivity: `streamstats` respects the event ordering presented to it, which means the preceding `sort` (or the natural _time-descending default of the base search) dictates behaviour. If the stream is unsorted or sorted the wrong way, the running totals are meaningless. Always precede `streamstats` with `| sort 0 _time` to guarantee chronological order.

**Schedule configuration** (`savedsearches.conf`):
```ini
[UC-22.9.2: Audit Finding Closure Rate Trending]
cron_schedule = 0 3 1 * *
dispatch.earliest_time = -90d
dispatch.latest_time = now
actions = summary_index
action.summary_index._name = summary_compliance
action.summary_index.marker = uc=22.9.2,reg=ISO_27001
```

## Step 3 — Validate deployment

**(a) Field extraction check:** Run the following to confirm the TA is extracting every field the detection relies on:

```spl
index=grc sourcetype=grc:audit_finding earliest=-1h
| fieldsummary
| where count=0
| table field
```

Any row returned is a field the TA claims to extract but isn't appearing in recent data — it's either a rename upstream, a TA version mismatch, or a data-format change.

**(b) Required-field presence:** This detection specifically needs: `finding_key`, `is_closed`, `mttr_days`, `wow_mttr_pct`. Run:

```spl
index=grc sourcetype=grc:audit_finding earliest=-1h
| head 100
| table finding_key, is_closed, mttr_days, wow_mttr_pct
```

Every row should have non-null values for the fields the detection's `where` clause filters on. Nulls cause silent drops in the result set.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Before enabling as a production alert, run the base search with the threshold removed and profile the distribution of `mttr_days`:

```spl
<base search> earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(mttr_days) as p50 perc90(mttr_days) as p90 perc99(mttr_days) as p99 max(mttr_days) as hi
```

The current threshold `0` should sit between p90 and p99 for a balanced signal-to-noise ratio. If it's below p50, expect heavy alert volume; if above p99, expect under-detection.

**(e) Negative test:** Generate a synthetic 'should not alert' event using the Splunk Sample Generator or a crafted `| makeresults` event and confirm the detection does NOT fire on it. A detection that fires on everything is equivalent to a detection that fires on nothing.

## Step 4 — Operationalize (dashboard and reporting)

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-22.9.2: ISO 27001 evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Dual-Axis Line (Open Vs Closed Counts) (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.

**Panel 2 — Area Chart (``open_smoothed``):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.

**Panel 3 — Line Chart (``mean_mttr_days``, ``mttr_trend``, ``mttr_forecast``):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.

**Panel 4 — Single-value KPI (``wow_mttr_pct``):** Place at top-left. Configure `underLabel` with the regulation clause (e.g. 'ISO 27001 current violation count') and set a red colour range for any non-zero value. A zero reading is the steady state for a healthy control.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting and regulation-specific caveats

**Search returns no results when violations are expected:** Verify time-window alignment, index existence, and field extractions in that order. Most 'missing results' are simpler configuration issues before they're detection-logic issues.

**Search times out:** Check the search job inspector (`Activity > Jobs > <this UC's last run> > Inspect`). The phase consuming the time (fetch, command, summary) indicates whether the issue is data-layer (too wide a window, unaccelerated datamodel), command-layer (expensive `transaction` or `eventstats`), or post-aggregation.


**ISO 27001-specific failure modes:**

• Statement of Applicability (SoA) drift: ISO 27001 requires a SoA listing which Annex A controls are applicable and which are excluded with justification. A detection for a control excluded in the SoA adds noise to the audit evidence pile; reconcile UC-to-SoA mapping annually. Maintain `iso27001_soa.csv` with current applicability.

• Context of the organisation (Cl. 4): controls calibrated for a 50-person company's threat model do not suit a 5000-person multinational's. Detection thresholds, log retention, and escalation paths must align with the organisation's ISMS scope — a single 'enterprise default' for ISO 27001 is a tell-tale sign of a cookie-cutter implementation.

• Internal audit programme (Cl. 9.2) evidence: detections that support internal audits must produce records that can be attached to audit evidence packs. Tag the alert payload with audit_cycle=YYYY-HN so evidence bundling is trivial.

• Management review inputs (Cl. 9.3): control effectiveness metrics must be reviewable at management review. A detection that only raises alerts (no trend metric) cannot be brought to the management meeting; schedule a companion report that produces trend data per control.

Companion SPL queries (originally embedded in `spl` field; kept here for operator reference, run separately):

Companion query 1:
```
index=grc OR index=compliance sourcetype="grc:audit_finding" earliest=-90d
| eval is_closed=if(match(status,"(?i)closed|resolved|verified"),1,0)
| where is_closed=1
| eval mttr_days=if(isnotnull(closed_time),(closed_time-_time)/86400,
    if(isnotnull(remediated_time),(remediated_time-_time)/86400,null()))
| where isnum(mttr_days) AND mttr_days>=0 AND mttr_days<365
| timechart span=1w avg(mttr_days) as mean_mttr_days perc95(mttr_days) as p95_mttr_days
| trendline sma4(mean_mttr_days) as mttr_trend
| streamstats window=2 global=f first(mean_mttr_days) as prev_w_mttr
| eval wow_mttr_pct=if(isnotnull(prev_w_mttr) AND prev_w_mttr>0,round(100*(mean_mttr_days-prev_w_mttr)/prev_w_mttr,1),null())
| predict mean_mttr_days as mttr_forecast algorithm=LLP future_timespan=2
```
